title: Is Gravity a Real Force or Merely a Geometrical Effect?
abstract: Whether gravitation should be regarded as a fundamental force or as a manifestation of spacetime geometry remains an interesting conceptual question in physics. In Newtonian mechanics, gravitation is described as a force acting between massive objects, whereas General Relativity describes gravitational phenomena in terms of spacetime curvature, with freely falling bodies following geodesics. With this fundamental difference, it is legitimate to ask whether gravity is a real force or not, and it is very common to receive from experts a somewhat condescending answer such as "Drop a rock on your foot and you will feel that the force is real". This paper does not attempt to determine whether gravity is fundamentally a force or a geometrical phenomenon. Rather, it questions whether commonly invoked everyday experiences provide valid grounds for deciding between these interpretations.
